items.text: Muse Video Prompt Format lock: Aspect ratio 16:9 (source 3840×2160, 30 fps; generate at 1920×1080, 30 fps) — the output MUST use exactly this 16:9 horizontal ratio; no cropping, no reframing, no letterbox change. Master (include with every clip): Identity & costume lock: One woman in her late twenties — a snake-tribe queen out of Chinese xianxia fantasy. Long straight black hair falling past her waist, a high elegant face with strong brow bones and deep-set eyes, red-gold eye makeup swept outward, dark red lips. Her crown is a circlet of intertwined golden snakes, their raised heads and tails radiating around her head like a halo of serpents. Long gold drop earrings with small pendants. Her gown is white and pale gold: a high lace collar, fitted embroidered bodice, and enormous sheer veil-sleeves and train panels of gauze that billow to many times her body's volume — the veils are a locked prop, present in every shot, never detaching, never turning into wings or ribbons. Photorealistic cinematic fantasy rendering. No design changes anywhere; the crown's snakes never move or multiply. World & scenes: Scene A (the only scene) — a vast candlelit palace hall in Chinese imperial style: rows of golden candelabra receding into haze, dark lacquered pillars, warm smoke in the air, polished floor reflecting the candle glow. Composition rules by shot type, locked for the whole film: in the wides she is 40–50 percent of frame height (8 percent in the single extreme wide); in close-up her face is 50–55 percent of frame height; the veils always occupy more frame area than she does. CAMERA — transcribed from the original: slow ceremonial moves only — gentle push-ins of about 10 percent and near-imperceptible drifts; no handheld shake, no quick reframing, no cuts inside a shot; every transition is a flash of flame or white light, except one single hard cut before the final shot. THE RHYTHM & FORCE: six shots in 30 seconds, an average of five seconds a shot — the cutting is slow and nothing ever rushes. Movement lives in the cloth and the light: the veils billow, curl and settle at monumental scale while the queen herself moves in centimeters — an eyelid lifting, a head bowing about 19 degrees, one slow head-turn across three seconds. If she gestures, walks, dances or performs, it is wrong. The power is scale and stillness: the room performs, she reigns. EMOTION ARC: remote majesty, unbroken — she never smiles in the entire film (the smile stays at absolute zero; any upturn of the mouth breaks the film). Clip 1 is profile reverie: lids half-lowered in flutter, opening as the head bows and re-levels, inner brows lifted — sorrow inside the authority. Clip 2 is emergence: eyes fully open, brows settled flat, command replacing reverie. Clip 4 is the verdict: the slow turn to a frontal gaze, chin slightly down, eyes looking up through her lashes straight into the lens, held to the fade. Lighting & grade: one light logic all film — low warm candlelight from the sides (hard little flames, soft haze diffusion) against a strong backlight that makes the sheer veils glow white-gold; high warm contrast, deep amber shadows, golden ceremonial grade; the veils are the brightest element in every frame. Sound: vast hall ambience, faint candle crackle, slow cloth movement in the air, a deep quiet under everything; no dialogue, no singing, no music. Clip 1 (source 0:00–0:10.7): [0.0–3.7s] Shot 1 — Wide, one slow push-in of about 10 percent: in the candlelit hall she stands at frame left and raises both arms outward and up; her enormous sheer veils lift with the arms and spread to either side like slow wings, catching the backlight and glowing; her body stays nearly still inside the cloth's motion. Avoid: the veils flapping fast, her walking or turning, extra figures in the hall.
